title.raw: 卷111 刑罰志七 Volume 111 Treatise 7: Criminal Punishment

sentences.zh: 二儀既判，彙品生焉，五才兼用，廢一不可。

translations.literal: Once the Two Principles were distinguished, the myriad kinds of things came into being; the five materials must all be used together—none may be discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Once Heaven and Earth were set apart, the myriad creatures arose; the five elements must all work in concert—none can be done without.

sentences.zh: 金木水火土，咸相愛惡。

translations.literal: Metal, wood, water, fire, and earth all have mutual love and hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Metal, wood, water, fire, and earth each attract and repel one another.

sentences.zh: 陰陽所育，稟氣呈形，鼓之以雷霆，潤之以雲雨，春夏以生長之，秋冬以殺藏之。

translations.literal: What yin and yang nurture receives qi and takes form; thunder drums upon them, cloud and rain moisten them; spring and summer foster growth, autumn and winter kill and store away.
translations.idiomatic: Nurtured by yin and yang, beings receive vital breath and take shape; thunder rouses them, clouds and rain nourish them; spring and summer bring growth, autumn and winter bring killing and storage.

sentences.zh: 斯則德刑之設，著自神道。

translations.literal: Thus the establishment of virtue and punishment is manifest from the divine way.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the pairing of virtue and punishment stems from the way of the spirits.

sentences.zh: 聖人處天地之間，率神祇之意。

translations.literal: The sage stands between Heaven and Earth, following the intent of the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The sage dwells between Heaven and Earth, carrying out the will of the gods.

sentences.zh: 生民有喜怒之性，哀樂之心，應感而動，動而逾變。

translations.literal: The living people have the nature of joy and anger and a heart for grief and pleasure; stirred by impressions they move, and once moved they change ever more.
translations.idiomatic: The people possess natures of joy and anger and hearts for sorrow and delight; stirred by what they feel, they act—and once they act, they change without cease.

sentences.zh: 淳化所陶，下以惇朴。

translations.literal: Through the molding of pure transformation, those below become honest and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Shaped by sincere transformation, those below grow honest and unadorned.

sentences.zh: 故異章服，畫衣冠，示耻申禁，而不敢犯。

translations.literal: Therefore distinctive dress and painted garments were made, showing shame and proclaiming prohibitions, so that they would not dare to transgress.
translations.idiomatic: Hence distinctive garb and painted robes were devised, displaying shame and announcing bans, so that none would dare to offend.

sentences.zh: 其流既銳，姦黠萌生。

translations.literal: When that current grew sharp, treachery and cunning arose.
translations.idiomatic: As custom grew keen, treachery and craftiness sprang up.

sentences.zh: 是以明法令，立刑賞。

translations.literal: Therefore laws and ordinances were clarified and punishments and rewards were established.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason statutes were made clear and punishments and rewards were set in place.

sentences.zh: 故書曰：「象以典刑，流宥五刑，鞭作官刑，扑作教刑，金作贖刑，怙終賊刑，眚災肆赦。

translations.literal: Hence the Book says: 'Punishments are set forth with illustrative models; banishment pardons the five punishments; whipping serves as official punishment; beating with rods serves as pedagogical punishment; metal serves as ransom punishment; those who persist to the end meet execution as robbers; blameless calamities are broadly pardoned.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Documents says: 'Punishments are displayed as models for all to see; exile may spare the five punishments; the lash is the official penalty; the rod is the corrective penalty; fines of metal redeem guilt; those who persist to the end are punished as villains; innocent sufferers of disaster receive full pardon.'

sentences.zh: 」舜命咎繇曰：「五刑有服，五服三就，五流有宅，五宅三居。

translations.literal: ' Shun ordered Gao Yao, saying: 'When the five punishments have their proper fulfillment, the five degrees of mourning have three places of arrival; the five degrees of exile have dwellings; the five dwellings have three residences.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Shun commanded Gao Yao: 'Let the five punishments achieve their proper effect; let the five degrees of mourning have three stages of fulfillment; let the five degrees of exile have fixed abodes; let the five abodes have three places of residence.'

sentences.zh: 」夏刑則大辟二百，臏辟三百，宮辟五百，劓墨各千。

translations.literal: ' Under Xia punishments there were two hundred grand executions, three hundred side executions, five hundred castrations, and a thousand each of nose-cutting and branding.
translations.idiomatic: ' Under the Xia code there were two hundred capital offenses, three hundred punishments of cutting off the kneecap, five hundred castrations, and a thousand each of nose-cutting and tattooing.

sentences.zh: 殷因於夏，蓋有損益。

translations.literal: Yin followed Xia, with some additions and subtractions.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin dynasty took over from the Xia, with some reductions and additions.

sentences.zh: 周禮：建三典，刑邦國，以五聽求民情，八議以申之，三刺以審之。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: Establish the Three Canons to punish states; use the five hearings to seek the people's hearts; the eight deliberations to explain them; the three examinations to verify them.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou prescribe: establish the Three Canons to punish the realm; use the five modes of hearing to discern the people's sentiments; apply the eight deliberations to clarify cases; use the three examinations to review judgments.

sentences.zh: 左嘉石，平罷民；

translations.literal: On the left, the Vie Stone to chasten idle people;
translations.idiomatic: On the left stood the Vie Stone, to admonish the idle;

sentences.zh: 右肺石，達窮民。

translations.literal: on the right, the Lung Stone to reach the destitute people.
translations.idiomatic: on the right stood the Lung Stone, to give voice to the destitute.

sentences.zh: 宥不識，宥過失，宥遺忘；

translations.literal: pardon ignorance, pardon excess, pardon forgetfulness;
translations.idiomatic: pardon those who did not know, pardon those who erred, pardon those who forgot;

sentences.zh: 赦幼弱，赦耄耋，赦惷愚。

translations.literal: pardon the young and weak, pardon the aged, pardon the stupid.
translations.idiomatic: pardon the young and frail, pardon the very old, pardon the dull-witted.

sentences.zh: 周道既衰，穆王荒耄，命呂侯度作祥刑，以詰四方，五刑之屬增矣。

translations.literal: When the Zhou way had declined, King Mu grew remiss in age; he ordered Marquis Lü to compose the Sagacious Punishments to instruct the four quarters—the categories of the five punishments increased.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou way had waned, King Mu in his dotage ordered Marquis Lü to draft the Sagacious Punishments to admonish the four quarters—and the categories of the five punishments grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 夫疑獄氾問，與眾共之，眾疑赦之，必察小大之比以成之。

translations.literal: Where doubtful cases are numerous, consult with the masses; if the masses are doubtful, pardon; one must examine the comparative gravity and lightness to complete the judgment.
translations.idiomatic: When doubtful cases abound, consult the people; if the people remain doubtful, grant pardon; one must weigh the relative severity and leniency before rendering judgment.

sentences.zh: 先王之愛民如此，刑成而不可變，故君子盡心焉。

translations.literal: The former kings loved the people thus; once punishment was fixed it could not be changed—therefore the gentleman gave it his full heart.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the love the former kings bore for the people; once a sentence was fixed it could not be altered—hence the gentleman devoted his utmost care to it.

sentences.zh: 逮於戰國，競任威刑，以相吞噬。

translations.literal: By the time of the Warring States, they vied in applying severe punishments to devour one another.
translations.idiomatic: By the Warring States period, states competed in wielding harsh punishments to swallow one another up.

sentences.zh: 商君以法經六篇，入說於秦，議參夷之誅，連相坐之法。

translations.literal: Lord Shang with his six chapters of the Law Classic entered Qin to present his doctrine, proposing punishments of tearing apart the body and mutual implication for associated guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shang brought his six chapters of the Law Classic into Qin to expound his views, advocating dismemberment and the law of collective punishment for kin and associates.

sentences.zh: 風俗凋薄，號為虎狼。

translations.literal: Customs grew thin and debased; they were called tigers and wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Morals grew thin and harsh; the Qin was called a land of tigers and wolves.

sentences.zh: 及於始皇，遂兼天下，毀先王之典，制挾書之禁，法繁於秋荼，網密於凝脂，姦偽並生，赭衣塞路，獄犴淹積，囹圄成市。

translations.literal: When it reached the First Emperor, he then unified all under Heaven, destroyed the canons of the former kings, established the prohibition on hidden books; laws were thicker than autumn dew, nets denser than congealed lard; falsehood and deceit arose together, convicts in ochre robes blocked the roads, prison cells piled up, and jails became markets.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Emperor came to power, he united the realm, abolished the institutions of the former kings, and imposed the ban on private book-keeping; statutes multiplied like autumn weeds, legal nets were tighter than congealed fat; fraud and perjury flourished together, convicts in ochre robes choked the highways, prisons overflowed, and the jails became marketplaces.

sentences.zh: 於是天下怨叛，十室而九。

translations.literal: Then all under Heaven rebelled in resentment; nine of ten households turned away.
translations.idiomatic: Then the realm seethed with resentment and revolt; nine households in ten turned against the throne.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入關，蠲削煩苛，致三章之約。

translations.literal: When Han's founding ancestor entered the passes, he abolished heavy impositions and established the covenant of three articles.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder entered the passes, he swept away oppressive laws and proclaimed the covenant of three articles.

sentences.zh: 文帝以仁厚，斷獄四百，幾致刑措。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen with his benevolence and thickness—cases judged at four hundred, nearly reaching the point where punishments were set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, renowned for his clemency, saw only four hundred cases a year—nearly reaching the ideal of laying punishments aside altogether.

sentences.zh: 孝武世以姦宄滋甚，增律五十餘篇。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Wu, because treachery grew severe, more than fifty articles were added to the laws.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Wu, as treachery and violence grew rampant, more than fifty new statutes were added.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，路溫舒上書曰：「夫獄者天下之命，書曰：與其殺不辜，寧失有罪。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan, Lu Wenshu submitted a memorial saying: 'Prisons are the fate of all under Heaven; the Book says: Rather than execute the innocent, better to let the guilty escape.'
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xuan's reign, Lu Wenshu submitted a memorial: 'Prisons hold the fate of the realm in their hands. The Book of Documents says: Better to let the guilty go free than to execute the innocent.'

sentences.zh: 今治獄吏，非不慈仁也。

translations.literal: Today's prison officials are not lacking in kindness and benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Today's prison officials are not without kindness.

sentences.zh: 上下相毆，以刻為明，深者獲公名，平者多後患。

translations.literal: Superiors and subordinates egg one another on; severity is taken as clarity; the harsh gain public renown, the lenient often suffer later troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors and subordinates drive one another on; harshness passes for competence; those who judge severely win praise, while those who judge fairly often suffer for it later.

sentences.zh: 故治獄吏皆欲人死，非憎人也，自安之道，在人之死。

translations.literal: Therefore prison officials all wish people to die—not because they hate people, but because their path to security lies in others' deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Hence prison officials all want their prisoners dead—not from hatred of mankind, but because their own safety lies in others' deaths.

sentences.zh: 夫人情安則樂生，痛則思死，捶楚之下，何求而不得。

translations.literal: Human nature when at ease delights in life; when in pain it longs for death—under beating and flogging, what confession could not be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: When people are at ease they cling to life; in pain they yearn for death—under the lash and the rod, what could they not be made to confess?

sentences.zh: 故囚人不勝痛，則飾辭以示人。

translations.literal: Therefore when prisoners cannot bear the pain, they dress up their words to show others.
translations.idiomatic: When prisoners can no longer endure the pain, they fabricate confessions to satisfy their interrogators.

sentences.zh: 吏治者利其然，則指導以明之；

translations.literal: Officials who handle cases profit from this and then guide them to make it clear;
translations.idiomatic: The officials in charge, profiting from this, steer the prisoners toward the desired confession;

sentences.zh: 上奏畏郤，則鍛練而周內之。

translations.literal: fearing rejection when submitting upward, they forge and refine the record and bind it round and tight.
translations.idiomatic: and fearing rejection when the case goes up, they forge the testimony and wrap the indictment tight.

sentences.zh: 雖咎繇聽之，猶以為死有餘罪。

translations.literal: Even if Gao Yao himself heard the case, he would still think death left guilt remaining.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Gao Yao himself presided over the trial, he would still deem the condemned guilty beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 文致之罪明也。

translations.literal: Because the crime wrought by literary embellishment is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Because the fabricated charges are all too clear.

sentences.zh: 故天下之患，莫深於獄。

translations.literal: Therefore among the troubles of all under Heaven, none is deeper than prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Thus among the afflictions of the realm, none runs deeper than the prisons.

sentences.zh: 」宣帝善之。

translations.literal: ' Emperor Xuan approved of it.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 痛乎！

translations.literal: Painful indeed!
translations.idiomatic: How lamentable!

sentences.zh: 獄吏之害也久矣。

translations.literal: The harm of prison officials has been long-standing.
translations.idiomatic: The harm done by prison officials has been longstanding.

sentences.zh: 故曰，古之立獄，所以求生；

translations.literal: Hence it is said: in antiquity prisons were established to preserve life;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: in antiquity prisons were established to save lives;

sentences.zh: 今之立獄，所以求殺人。

translations.literal: today's prisons are established to seek people's deaths.
translations.idiomatic: today's prisons exist to procure deaths.

sentences.zh: 不可不慎也。

translations.literal: One cannot but be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: This cannot be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 于定國為廷尉，集諸法律，凡九百六十卷，大辟四百九十條，千八百八十二事，死罪決比，凡三千四百七十二條，[1]諸斷罪當用者，合二萬六千二百七十二條。

translations.literal: Yu Dingguo as Minister of Justice collected all laws—nine hundred sixty volumes in all, four hundred ninety articles of grand execution, one thousand eight hundred eighty-two matters; death-sentence precedents totaled three thousand four hundred seventy-two articles; all articles applicable to judgment totaled twenty-six thousand two hundred seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Dingguo served as Minister of Justice, he compiled all statutes into nine hundred sixty volumes: four hundred ninety capital offenses, one thousand eight hundred eighty-two specific cases, and three thousand four hundred seventy-two death-sentence precedents—in all, twenty-six thousand two hundred seventy-two articles governing criminal judgment.

sentences.zh: 後漢二百年間，律章無大增減。

translations.literal: Throughout the two hundred years of Later Han, the statutes saw no great increase or decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Over the two hundred years of Later Han, the legal code underwent no major changes.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝造甲子科條，犯釱左右趾者，易以斗械。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei created the Jiazi Code articles; those who violated the foot-shackle on left or right toe had it replaced with cangue and fetters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei drafted the Jiazi Code; offenders subject to foot-shackles on either leg were instead punished with the cangue and fetters.

sentences.zh: 明帝改士民罰金之坐，除婦人加笞之制。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming changed the penalty of fines for gentry and commoners and abolished the added flogging for women.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming revised the fine penalties for commoners and gentry and abolished the extra flogging imposed on women.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝以魏制峻密，又詔車騎賈充集諸儒學，刪定名例，為二十卷，并合二千九百餘條。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin, because Wei's system was harsh and dense, again ordered Cavalry General Jia Chong to gather the Confucian scholars, revise and fix the statutes and precedents into twenty volumes, totaling more than twenty-nine hundred articles.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the Wei code overly harsh and intricate, Emperor Wu of Jin ordered Cavalry General Jia Chong to assemble Confucian scholars to revise the statutes and precedents into twenty volumes comprising more than twenty-nine hundred articles.

sentences.zh: 晉室喪亂，中原蕩然。

translations.literal: The Jin house fell into disorder; the Central Plains were swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin dynasty collapsed into chaos, and the Central Plains were laid waste.

sentences.zh: 魏氏承百王之末，屬崩散之後，典刑泯棄，禮俗澆薄。

translations.literal: The Wei house inherited the end of a hundred kings, belonging to the time after collapse and dispersal—canonical punishments were lost, rites and customs thin and debased.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei arose at the end of a long line of dynasties, in the aftermath of collapse and dispersal; canonical punishments were abandoned and rites and customs had grown thin.

sentences.zh: 自太祖撥亂，蕩滌華夏，至于太和，然後吏清政平，斷獄省簡，所謂百年而後勝殘去殺。

translations.literal: From when the Grand Ancestor quelled disorder and swept clean the Hua-xia, until the Taihe era, only then were officials pure and government level, cases judged with simplicity—what is called 'after a hundred years, overcoming cruelty and removing killing.'
translations.idiomatic: From the Grand Ancestor's pacification of chaos and cleansing of the realm until the Taihe era, officials grew upright, government grew fair, and litigation grew sparse—the fulfillment of the saying that only after a century does a state overcome cruelty and abolish capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 故榷舉行事，以著于篇。

translations.literal: Therefore relevant deeds are selected and set forth in this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the salient measures are gathered here and recorded in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 魏初，禮俗純朴，刑禁疏簡。

translations.literal: In early Wei, rites and customs were pure and plain, punishments and prohibitions sparse and simple.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wei period, customs were plain and punishments few.

sentences.zh: 宣帝南遷，復置四部大人，坐王庭決辭訟，以言語約束，刻契記事，無囹圄考訊之法，諸犯罪者，皆臨時決遣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan moved south, he again established the four division chieftains, who sat in the royal court to decide lawsuits, using verbal agreements for restraint and carved tokens to record matters; there were no methods of prison interrogation—all offenders were decided and dispatched on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan moved south, he reinstated the four division chieftains, who sat in the royal court to settle disputes, relying on verbal agreements and carved tokens to record matters; there was no system of prison interrogation—offenders were judged and punished on the spot.

sentences.zh: 神元因循，亡所革易。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenyuan followed along without any reforms.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenyuan followed precedent without change.

sentences.zh: 穆帝時，劉聰、石勒傾覆晉室。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Mu, Liu Cong and Shi Le overthrew the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Mu, Liu Cong and Shi Le brought down the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 帝將平其亂，乃峻刑法，每以軍令從事。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to quell their disorder and therefore made punishments severe, always applying military law.
translations.idiomatic: Intent on quelling the turmoil, the emperor tightened criminal law and routinely applied military justice.

sentences.zh: 民乘寬政，多以違命得罪，死者以萬計。

translations.literal: The people, accustomed to lenient government, mostly offended through disobeying orders; the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Accustomed to lenient rule, the people often fell afoul of strict commands; the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 於是國落騷駭。

translations.literal: Then the tribes of the realm were stirred in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples were thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 平文承業，綏集離散。

translations.literal: Emperor Pingwen inherited the enterprise and pacified and gathered the scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Pingwen took up the mantle and pacified the scattered populace.

sentences.zh: 昭成建國二年：當死者，聽其家獻金馬以贖；

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianguo under Emperor Zhaocheng: those who should die were permitted to have their families offer gold and horses to ransom them;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianguo under Emperor Zhaocheng: those sentenced to death might have their families ransom them with gold and horses;

sentences.zh: 犯大逆者，親族男女無少長皆斬；

translations.literal: those who committed great treason—men and women of the kindred, none spared young or old, all were beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: those guilty of great treason—men and women of the clan, young and old alike, were all beheaded;

sentences.zh: 男女不以禮交皆死；

translations.literal: men and women who consorted without ritual propriety were all put to death;
translations.idiomatic: men and women who consorted without proper ritual all faced death;

sentences.zh: 民相殺者，聽與死家馬牛四十九頭，及送葬器物以平之；

translations.literal: when commoners killed one another, they were permitted to give the victim's family forty-nine head of horses and cattle and funeral goods to settle the matter;
translations.idiomatic: when commoners killed one another, the killer might settle the case by paying the victim's family forty-nine head of livestock plus funeral goods;

sentences.zh: 無繫訊連逮之坐；

translations.literal: there was no punishment of imprisonment, interrogation, or chain arrest;
translations.idiomatic: there was no imprisonment, interrogation, or chain liability;

sentences.zh: 盜官物，一備五，私則備十。

translations.literal: for theft of official goods, restitution at fivefold; for private goods, tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: theft of government property required fivefold restitution; theft of private property, tenfold.

sentences.zh: 法令明白，百姓晏然。

translations.literal: Laws and ordinances were clear; the common people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The laws were clear, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 太祖幼遭艱難，備嘗險阻，具知民之情偽。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor in youth suffered hardship and fully tasted danger; he thoroughly knew the people's true and false hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor endured hardship in his youth and knew every peril; he understood the people's hearts in full.

sentences.zh: 及在位，躬行仁厚，協和民庶。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, he personally practiced benevolence and thickness and harmonized the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the throne, he personally practiced benevolence and brought harmony to the people.

sentences.zh: 既定中原，患前代刑網峻密，乃命三公郎王德除其法之酷切於民者，約定科令，大崇簡易。

translations.literal: Once the Central Plains were secured, troubled by the previous dynasty's harsh and dense penal net, he ordered Secretariat Attendant Wang De to remove from the laws what was cruel and cutting toward the people, fix the statutes, and greatly promote simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: After securing the Central Plains, troubled by the harsh legal nets of earlier dynasties, he ordered Secretariat Attendant Wang De to strip away laws oppressive to the people, codify new statutes, and promote simplicity above all.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下民久苦兵亂，畏法樂安。

translations.literal: At that time the people of all under Heaven had long suffered military disorder and feared the law yet delighted in peace.
translations.idiomatic: By then the people had long suffered war and chaos; they feared harsh law but welcomed peace.

sentences.zh: 帝知其若此，乃鎮之以玄默，罰必從輕，兆庶欣戴焉。

translations.literal: The emperor knew it was thus and therefore governed them with deep silence; punishments were always light, and the myriad people rejoiced in support.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing this, the emperor governed with quiet restraint, always leaning toward leniency in punishment, and the people rejoiced in his rule.

sentences.zh: 然於大臣持法不捨。

translations.literal: Yet toward great ministers he held to the law without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Yet toward high officials he showed no leniency in enforcing the law.

sentences.zh: 季年災異屢見，太祖不豫，綱紀褫頓，刑罰頗為濫酷。

translations.literal: In his final years calamities and portents appeared repeatedly; the Grand Ancestor fell ill, discipline collapsed, and punishments grew somewhat excessive and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years, as omens multiplied and the Grand Ancestor fell ill, discipline slackened and punishments grew unduly harsh.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，修廢官，恤民隱，命南平公長孫嵩、北新侯安同對理民訟，庶政復有敍焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, he restored abolished offices and showed compassion for the people's hidden grievances; he ordered Duke of Nanping Changgunsun Song and Marquis of Beixin An Tong jointly to handle the people's lawsuits, and common administration regained order.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, he restored abolished offices and attended to the people's hidden grievances, appointing Duke of Nanping Changgunsun Song and Marquis of Beixin An Tong to hear civil suits jointly—and government regained its order.

sentences.zh: 帝既練精庶事，為吏者浸以深文避罪。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had refined his mastery of common affairs, officials gradually used harsh literary constructions to avoid blame.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor grew adept at governance, officials increasingly twisted the law to shield themselves from blame.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，以刑禁重，神䴥中，詔司徒崔浩定律令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, because punishments and prohibitions were heavy, in the Shengui era he ordered Minister of Works Cui Hao to fix the laws and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu ascended the throne, finding punishments too severe, he ordered Minister of Works Cui Hao to codify the laws during the Shengui era.

sentences.zh: 除五歲四歲刑，增一年刑。

translations.literal: The five-year and four-year punishments were abolished and a one-year punishment was added.
translations.idiomatic: The five- and four-year terms of penal servitude were abolished and replaced with a one-year term.

sentences.zh: 分大辟為二科死，斬死，入絞。

translations.literal: Grand execution was divided into two categories of death: decapitation and death by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment was divided into two degrees: decapitation and strangulation.

sentences.zh: 大逆不道腰斬，誅其同籍，年十四已下腐刑，女子沒縣官。

translations.literal: Great treason and impiety were punished by cutting at the waist; those of the same household register were executed; those fourteen and below received castration; women were confiscated to the district office.
translations.idiomatic: Great treason was punished by execution at the waist; kin of the same household register were put to death; males fourteen and under were castrated; women were enslaved to the district authorities.

sentences.zh: 害其親者轘之。

translations.literal: Those who harmed their kin were torn apart by chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Those who harmed their kin were torn apart by chariots.

sentences.zh: 為蠱毒者，男女皆斬，而焚其家。

translations.literal: Those who practiced gu poison—men and women were all beheaded and their households burned.
translations.idiomatic: Practitioners of gu sorcery—men and women alike were beheaded and their homes burned.

sentences.zh: 巫蠱者，負羖羊抱犬沉諸淵。

translations.literal: Sorcerers of gu were made to carry a ram on their back and hold a dog as they were drowned in the deep.
translations.idiomatic: Sorcerers who practiced gu were made to carry a ram on their backs and hold a dog as they were drowned in the depths.

sentences.zh: 當刑者贖，貧則加鞭二百。

translations.literal: Those who should be punished might ransom themselves; if poor, two hundred lashes were added.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders might commute their sentences by ransom; the poor received two hundred lashes instead.

sentences.zh: 畿內民富者燒炭於山，貧者役於圊溷，女子入舂槀；

translations.literal: Within the capital region, the wealthy burned charcoal in the mountains, the poor labored in privies, women were sent to pound grain;
translations.idiomatic: Within the capital region, wealthy offenders burned charcoal in the mountains, poor offenders labored in privies, and women were sent to pound grain;

sentences.zh: 其固疾不逮于人，守苑囿。

translations.literal: those with chronic illness who could not keep pace with others guarded the parks and preserves.
translations.idiomatic: those with chronic illness who could not keep pace with others were assigned to guard the imperial parks.

sentences.zh: 王官階九品，得以官爵除刑。

translations.literal: Officials of the royal court in nine ranks could use office and enfeoffment to commute punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials of the nine ranks could commute punishment through their office and noble rank.

sentences.zh: 婦人當刑而孕，產後百日乃決。

translations.literal: Women who should be punished but were pregnant—sentence was carried out a hundred days after childbirth.
translations.idiomatic: Pregnant women due for punishment were not sentenced until a hundred days after giving birth.

sentences.zh: 年十四已下，降刑之半，八十及九歲，非殺人不坐。

translations.literal: Those fourteen and below had punishments reduced by half; at eighty and ninety years, except for homicide they were not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Those fourteen and under received half the normal sentence; those eighty or ninety were not punished except for murder.

sentences.zh: 拷訊不踰四十九。

translations.literal: Interrogation by torture did not exceed forty-nine blows.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation under torture was limited to forty-nine strokes.

sentences.zh: 論刑者，部主具狀，公車鞫辭，而三都決之。

translations.literal: In discussing punishment, the department head prepared the report, the Imperial Carriage Office examined the testimony, and the Three Capitals decided it.
translations.idiomatic: In capital cases, the department head prepared the dossier, the Imperial Carriage Office examined testimony, and the Three Capitals rendered judgment.

sentences.zh: 當死者，部案奏聞。

translations.literal: Those who should die—the department case was submitted for the emperor's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Death sentences were reported to the throne by the department.

sentences.zh: 以死不可復生，懼監官不能平，獄成皆呈，帝親臨問，無異辭怨言乃絕之。

translations.literal: Because death cannot be restored to life, fearing that supervising officials could not judge fairly, when cases were complete all were presented; the emperor personally questioned them, and only when there were no differing words or complaints of injustice was execution carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Because the dead cannot be restored to life, and fearing that officials might judge unfairly, completed cases were all presented to the emperor, who questioned the prisoners personally; only when there were no protests or complaints of injustice was the sentence carried out.

sentences.zh: 諸州國之大辟，皆先讞報乃施行。

translations.literal: Grand executions in all provinces and states were first reported for approval before being carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Capital sentences in the provinces were all reported for approval before execution.

sentences.zh: 闕左懸登聞鼓，人有窮冤則撾鼓，公車上奏其表。

translations.literal: To the left of the palace gate was hung the Drum for Hearing Grievances; when people had desperate wrongs they struck the drum and the Imperial Carriage Office submitted their petition.
translations.idiomatic: To the left of the palace gate hung the Drum for Hearing Grievances; those with desperate grievances struck it, and the Imperial Carriage Office forwarded their petitions to the throne.

sentences.zh: 是後民官瀆貨，帝思有以肅之。

translations.literal: After this, local officials took bribes, and the emperor thought to discipline them sternly.
translations.idiomatic: After this, local officials grew corrupt through bribery, and the emperor sought a way to restore discipline.

sentences.zh: 太延三年，詔天下吏民，得舉告牧守之不法。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiyan, an edict proclaimed to officials and people throughout the realm that they might report the unlawful conduct of prefects and governors.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiyan, an edict allowed officials and commoners throughout the empire to report unlawful conduct by prefects and governors.

sentences.zh: 於是凡庶之凶悖者，專求牧宰之失，迫脅在位，取豪於閭閻。

translations.literal: Thereupon the violent and rebellious among the common folk devoted themselves to seeking the faults of local administrators, coerced those in office, and extracted wealth from the neighborhoods.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon violent and unruly commoners devoted themselves to hunting for administrators' faults, coerced officials, and extorted wealth from their neighborhoods.

sentences.zh: 而長吏咸降心以待之，苟免而不耻，貪暴猶自若也。

translations.literal: Senior officials all lowered themselves humbly to await this, seeking merely to escape without shame, and remained as greedy and violent as before.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials all humbled themselves before accusers, seeking only to escape censure without shame, and remained as greedy and violent as ever.

sentences.zh: 時輿駕數親征討及行幸四方，真君五年，命恭宗總百揆監國。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial carriage frequently went on campaigns in person and on tours to the four quarters; in the fifth year of Zhenjun, the emperor ordered Emperor Gongzong to oversee all government affairs and supervise the state.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor frequently led campaigns in person and toured the realm; in the fifth year of Zhenjun he ordered Emperor Gongzong to oversee all government affairs and govern the state.

sentences.zh: 少傅游雅上疏曰：「殿下親覽百揆，經營內外，昧旦而興，諮詢國老。

translations.literal: Junior Tutor You Ya submitted a memorial saying: "Your Highness personally reviews all government affairs, manages internal and external affairs, rises before dawn, and consults the elders of state."
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor You Ya submitted a memorial saying: "Your Highness personally oversees all government affairs, manages internal and external matters, rises before dawn, and consults the state's elders."

sentences.zh: 臣職忝疑承，司是獻替。

translations.literal: Your servant's office unworthily bears the duty of counsel and is charged with offering remonstrance and improvement.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's office unworthily bears the duty of counsel and is charged with offering remonstrance and improvement.

sentences.zh: 漢武時，始啟河右四郡，議諸疑罪而謫徙之。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Han, the four commanderies west of the Yellow River were first opened, and it was proposed that all doubtful crimes be punished by banishment and forced relocation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Han, the four commanderies west of the Yellow River were first opened, and it was proposed that doubtful crimes be punished by exile and forced relocation.

sentences.zh: 十數年後，邊郡充實，並修農戍，孝宣因之，以服北方。

translations.literal: After more than ten years, the frontier commanderies were filled and strengthened with farming and garrison duty; Emperor Xuan followed this policy and thereby subdued the north.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years the frontier commanderies were fully settled and fortified with farming and garrison duty; Emperor Xuan followed this policy and thereby pacified the north.

sentences.zh: 此近世之事也。

translations.literal: This is a matter of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: This is a matter of recent history.

sentences.zh: 帝王之於罪人，非怒而誅之，欲其徙善而懲惡。

translations.literal: When emperors and kings deal with criminals, it is not in anger that they execute them, but to move them toward goodness and punish evil.
translations.idiomatic: When emperors and kings punish criminals, they do not execute them in anger, but to move them toward goodness and punish evil.

sentences.zh: 謫徙之苦，其懲亦深。

translations.literal: The hardship of banishment and relocation is also a deep punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The hardship of exile and forced relocation is itself a severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 自非大逆正刑，皆可從徙，雖舉家投遠，忻喜赴路，力役終身，不敢言苦。

translations.literal: Except for capital punishment for great treason, all may follow relocation; even if whole families were sent far away, they would go gladly on the road, labor for life, and dare not speak of hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from capital punishment for great treason, all offenders could be sentenced to relocation; even whole families sent far away would set out gladly, labor for life, and dare not complain of hardship.

sentences.zh: 且遠流分離，心或思善。

translations.literal: Moreover, sent far away and separated, their hearts may turn toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, sent far away and separated from home, they may turn their hearts toward goodness.

sentences.zh: 如此，姦邪可息，邊垂足備。

translations.literal: In this way wickedness may cease, and the frontier may be fully defended.
translations.idiomatic: In this way wickedness may be checked and the frontier fully defended.

sentences.zh: 」恭宗善其言，然未之行。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gongzong approved his words, but did not put them into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gongzong approved his proposal, but did not carry it out.

sentences.zh: 六年春，以有司斷法不平，詔諸疑獄皆付中書，依古經義論決之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, because the responsible offices judged the law unfairly, an edict ordered that all doubtful cases be entrusted to the Central Secretariat and decided according to ancient canonical principles.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year, because responsible offices judged cases unfairly, an edict ordered that all doubtful cases be referred to the Central Secretariat and decided according to ancient canonical principles.

sentences.zh: 初盜律，贓四十匹致大辟，民多慢政，峻其法，贓三匹皆死。

translations.literal: At first the theft law fixed death for forty bolts of stolen goods; the people widely scorned government, so the law was made severe, and three bolts of stolen goods brought death to all.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the theft law imposed death for forty bolts of stolen goods; because the people widely scorned government, the law was tightened so that theft of three bolts brought death.

sentences.zh: 正平元年，詔曰：「刑網大密，犯者更眾，朕甚愍之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengping, an edict said: "The penal net is too dense, and offenders are ever more numerous; We are deeply troubled by this."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengping, an edict said: "The penal net is too dense, and offenders grow ever more numerous; We are deeply troubled by this."

sentences.zh: 其詳案律令，務求厥中，有不便於民者增損之。

translations.literal: Let the statutes and commands be examined in detail, striving to find the mean; where anything is inconvenient for the people, add to or reduce it.
translations.idiomatic: Examine the statutes and commands in detail and strive for the proper mean; where anything burdens the people, revise it accordingly.

sentences.zh: 」於是游雅與中書侍郎胡方回等改定律制。

translations.literal: " Thereupon You Ya, together with Secretariat Gentleman Hu Fanghui and others, revised the legal system.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon You Ya, together with Secretariat Gentleman Hu Fanghui and others, revised the legal code.

sentences.zh: 盜律復舊，加故縱、通情、止舍之法及他罪，凡三百九十一條。

translations.literal: The theft law was restored to its former standard, and laws on knowingly allowing crime, communicating intelligence, harboring offenders, and other offenses were added, totaling three hundred and ninety-one articles.
translations.idiomatic: The theft law was restored to its former standard, and provisions on knowingly allowing crime, communicating intelligence, harboring offenders, and other offenses were added, for a total of three hundred and ninety-one articles.

sentences.zh: 門誅四，大辟一百四十五，刑二百二十一條。

translations.literal: Clan executions: four; capital punishments: one hundred and forty-five; lesser punishments: two hundred and twenty-one articles.
translations.idiomatic: There were four articles on clan execution, one hundred and forty-five on capital punishment, and two hundred and twenty-one on lesser punishments.

sentences.zh: 有司雖增損條章，猶未能闡明刑典。

translations.literal: Although the responsible offices added to and reduced the articles, they still could not fully clarify the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: Although the responsible offices revised the articles, they still could not fully clarify the penal code.

sentences.zh: 高宗初，仍遵舊式。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign, the former system was still followed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign, the former system was still followed.

sentences.zh: 太安四年，始設酒禁。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tai'an, a prohibition on wine was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tai'an, a prohibition on wine was first established.

sentences.zh: 是時年穀屢登，士民多因酒致酗訟，或議主政。

translations.literal: At that time harvests were repeatedly abundant, and gentry and commoners often through wine caused drunken brawls and lawsuits, or debated and criticized government.
translations.idiomatic: At that time harvests were repeatedly abundant, and gentry and commoners often through wine caused drunken brawls and lawsuits, or debated and criticized government policy.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其若此，故一切禁之，釀、沽飲皆斬之，吉凶賓親，則開禁，有日程。

translations.literal: The emperor hated matters such as these, and therefore banned them entirely; brewing, selling, and drinking were all punished by decapitation; for auspicious and inauspicious rites and guest receptions, the ban was lifted according to a fixed schedule.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated such conduct and banned wine entirely; brewing, selling, and drinking were all punishable by decapitation; for weddings, funerals, and guest receptions the ban was lifted on fixed days.

sentences.zh: 增置內外候官，伺察諸曹外部州鎮，至有微服雜亂於府寺間，以求百官疵失。

translations.literal: Surveillance officials were added inside and outside the court to spy on all offices and on external provinces and garrisons, even to the point of going in disguise and mingling among government offices to seek out officials' faults.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance officials were added inside and outside the court to spy on all offices and on provinces and garrisons, even mingling in disguise among government compounds to uncover officials' faults.

sentences.zh: 其所窮治，有司苦加訊惻，而多相誣逮，輒劾以不敬。

translations.literal: In cases they pursued to the end, the responsible offices harshly applied interrogation and torture, and many falsely implicated one another; they were then charged with disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: In cases they pursued to the end, responsible offices applied harsh interrogation and torture, and many falsely implicated one another; they were then charged with disrespect.

sentences.zh: 諸司官贓二丈皆斬。

translations.literal: Officials in all offices who took bribes of two zhang of silk were all decapitated.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in all offices who accepted bribes of two zhang of silk were all decapitated.

sentences.zh: 又增律七十九章，門房之誅十有三，大辟三十五，刑六十二。

translations.literal: Seventy-nine articles were also added to the law: thirteen on clan execution, thirty-five capital punishments, and sixty-two lesser punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-nine articles were also added to the law: thirteen on clan execution, thirty-five capital punishments, and sixty-two lesser punishments.

sentences.zh: 和平末，冀州刺史源賀上言：「自非大逆手殺人者，請原其命，謫守邊戍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Heping era, Jizhou Inspector Yuan He submitted a memorial saying: "Except for great treason and homicide by one's own hand, We ask that their lives be spared and they be banished to guard the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Heping era, Jizhou Inspector Yuan He submitted a memorial saying: "Except for great treason and homicide by one's own hand, We ask that their lives be spared and they be banished to guard the frontier."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 顯祖即位，除口誤，開酒禁。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu acceded to the throne, punishment for verbal slips was abolished and the prohibition on wine was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu acceded to the throne, punishment for verbal slips was abolished and the prohibition on wine was lifted.

sentences.zh: 帝勤於治功，百僚內外，莫不震肅。

translations.literal: The emperor was diligent in governing achievements, and among all officials within and without, none failed to be awed into discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was diligent in governing, and officials throughout the court and the provinces were all awed into discipline.

sentences.zh: 及傳位高祖，猶躬覽萬機，刑政嚴明，顯拔清節，沙汰貪鄙。

translations.literal: Even after abdicating to Emperor Gaozu, he still personally reviewed the myriad affairs of state; penal policy was strict and clear, the upright and incorruptible were prominently promoted, and the greedy and base were sifted out.
translations.idiomatic: Even after abdicating to Emperor Gaozu, he still personally oversaw state affairs; penal policy was strict and clear, the upright and incorruptible were promoted, and the greedy and base were weeded out.

sentences.zh: 牧守之廉潔者，往往有聞焉。

translations.literal: Prefects and governors who were honest and clean were often heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Reports of honest and incorruptible prefects and governors became common.

sentences.zh: 延興四年，詔自非大逆干紀者，皆止其身，罷門房之誅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanxing, an edict declared that except for great treason and violation of fundamental norms, punishment would stop with the offender himself, and clan execution was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yanxing, an edict declared that except for great treason and violation of fundamental norms, punishment would stop with the offender himself and clan execution was abolished.

sentences.zh: 自獄付中書覆案，後頗上下法，遂罷之，獄有大疑，乃平議焉。

translations.literal: Since cases had been entrusted to the Central Secretariat for review, later the law was often applied differently for superiors and inferiors, and this was therefore abolished; only when a case raised great doubt was it jointly deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: Since cases had been referred to the Central Secretariat for review, the law was later often applied differently for officials and commoners, and this practice was therefore abolished; only cases of grave doubt were jointly deliberated.

sentences.zh: 先是諸曹奏事，多有疑請，又口傳詔敕，或致矯擅。

translations.literal: Previously, when the various offices submitted business, there were many requests for clarification of doubtful points, and edicts were also transmitted orally, sometimes leading to usurpation and abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when the various offices submitted business, they often requested clarification of doubtful points, and edicts were also transmitted orally, sometimes leading to usurpation and abuse.

sentences.zh: 於是事無大小，皆令據律正名，不得疑奏。

translations.literal: Thereupon, whether matters were great or small, all were ordered to be decided according to the law by proper designation, and doubtful submissions were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, whether matters were great or small, all were ordered to be decided strictly according to law, and doubtful submissions were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 合則制可，失衷則彈詰之，盡從中墨詔。

translations.literal: If correct, approval was granted; if wrong, censure was applied—all according to edicts from the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: If correct, approval was granted; if wrong, censure followed—all by edicts from the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自是事咸精詳，下莫敢相罔。

translations.literal: From this time all business was handled with precision and detail, and subordinates did not dare deceive one another.
translations.idiomatic: From this time all business was handled with precision and detail, and subordinates did not dare deceive one another.

sentences.zh: 顯祖末年，尤重刑罰，言及常用惻愴。

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Xianzu, he especially emphasized penal punishment, and whenever he spoke of it he was deeply moved with compassion.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Emperor Xianzu, he especially emphasized penal punishment, and whenever he spoke of it he was deeply moved with compassion.

sentences.zh: 每於獄案，必令覆鞫，諸有囚繫，或積年不斷。

translations.literal: In every criminal case he ordered re-examination; among all prisoners held, some went unresolved for years.
translations.idiomatic: In every criminal case he ordered re-examination, and some prisoners remained detained for years without resolution.

sentences.zh: 羣臣頗以為言。

translations.literal: The ministers often spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers often raised the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「獄滯雖非治體，不猶愈乎倉卒而濫也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Delay in cases is not the proper way to govern, but is it not still better than hasty and indiscriminate judgment?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Delay in cases is not ideal governance, but is it not still better than hasty and indiscriminate judgment?"

sentences.zh: 夫人幽苦則思善，故囹圄與福堂同居。

translations.literal: When people suffer in darkness and hardship, they turn toward goodness; therefore prison and the hall of blessing dwell together.
translations.idiomatic: When people suffer in darkness and hardship, they turn toward goodness; therefore prison and the hall of blessing dwell together.

sentences.zh: 朕欲其改悔，而加以輕恕耳。

translations.literal: We wish them to reform and repent, and therefore add leniency and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: We wish them to reform and repent, and therefore show leniency and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 」由是囚繫雖淹滯，而刑罰多得其所。

translations.literal: " From this, although prisoners were long detained, punishments mostly matched their offenses.
translations.idiomatic: From this, although prisoners were long detained, punishments mostly fit the offenses.

sentences.zh: 又以赦令屢下，則狂愚多僥幸，故自延興，終於季年，不復下赦。

translations.literal: Also, because amnesty edicts were repeatedly issued, the reckless and foolish often hoped for luck; therefore from Yanxing until the end of his reign, amnesties were no longer issued.
translations.idiomatic: Also, because amnesty edicts were repeatedly issued, the reckless and foolish often hoped for luck; therefore from Yanxing until the end of his reign, no further amnesties were issued.

sentences.zh: 理官鞫囚，杖限五十，而有司欲免之則以細捶，欲陷之則先大杖。

translations.literal: When judicial officials interrogated prisoners, the limit for beating was fifty strokes, but if the responsible offices wished to exonerate someone they used fine rods, and if they wished to trap someone they first applied heavy cudgels.
translations.idiomatic: When judicial officials interrogated prisoners, the beating limit was fifty strokes, but if responsible offices wished to exonerate someone they used light rods, and if they wished to trap someone they first applied heavy cudgels.

sentences.zh: 民多不勝而誣引，或絕命於杖下。

translations.literal: Many people could not endure it and falsely confessed, or lost their lives under the rods.
translations.idiomatic: Many could not endure it and falsely confessed, or lost their lives under the rods.

sentences.zh: 顯祖知其若此，乃為之制。

sentences.zh: 皆從於輕簡也。

translations.literal: All followed the lighter and simpler standard.
translations.idiomatic: All followed the lighter and simpler standard.

sentences.zh: 三年，下詔曰：「治因政寬，弊由網密。

translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an edict said: "Good governance arises from lenient policy, and abuses arise from a dense penal net."

sentences.zh: 今候職千數，姦巧弄威，重罪受賕不列，細過吹毛而舉。

translations.literal: Now the surveillance posts number in the thousands; the cunning wield power, serious crimes involving bribes go unreported, and trivial faults are prosecuted by nitpicking.
translations.idiomatic: Now surveillance posts number in the thousands; the cunning wield power, serious bribery goes unreported, and trivial faults are prosecuted by nitpicking.

sentences.zh: 其一切罷之。

translations.idiomatic: Let them all be abolished at once.

translations.idiomatic: Thereupon several hundred upright and diligent men were newly appointed to prevent brawling in the streets.

sentences.zh: 吏民安其職業。

translations.literal: Officials and people were secure in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners were secure in their occupations.

sentences.zh: 先是以律令不具，姦吏用法，致有輕重。

translations.literal: Previously, because the statutes and commands were incomplete, corrupt officials manipulated the law and caused punishments to vary in severity.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, because the statutes and commands were incomplete, corrupt officials manipulated the law and caused punishments to vary in severity.

sentences.zh: 詔中書令高閭集中祕官等修改舊文，隨例增減。

translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Secretariat Director Gao Lü, together with officials of the Imperial Library and others, to revise the old text and add or reduce articles according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 又敕羣官，參議厥衷，經御刊定。

translations.literal: All officials were also commanded to discuss the proper mean, and after imperial review it was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: All officials were also commanded to discuss the proper mean, and after imperial review the code was fixed.

sentences.zh: 五年冬訖，凡八百三十二章，門房之誅十有六，大辟之罪二百三十五，刑三百七十七；

translations.literal: By the winter of the fifth year it was complete: eight hundred and thirty-two articles in all, sixteen on clan execution, two hundred and thirty-five capital crimes, and three hundred and seventy-seven lesser punishments;
translations.idiomatic: By the winter of the fifth year it was complete: eight hundred and thirty-two articles in all, sixteen on clan execution, two hundred and thirty-five capital crimes, and three hundred and seventy-seven lesser punishments;

sentences.zh: 除羣行剽劫首謀門誅，律重者止梟首。

translations.literal: except for gang robbery and plunder whose ringleaders were subject to clan execution, where the law was severe punishment was limited to decapitation and display.
translations.idiomatic: except for gang robbery and plunder whose ringleaders were subject to clan execution, severe punishments were limited to decapitation and public display.

sentences.zh: 時法官及州郡縣不能以情折獄。

translations.idiomatic: At that time judges and the offices of provinces, commanderies, and counties could not decide cases according to circumstances.

translations.idiomatic: they therefore made heavy cangues nearly a full arm-span around;

translations.idiomatic: they also hung stones by rope from the prisoner's neck, injuring the flesh down to the bone;

sentences.zh: 更使壯卒迭搏之。

translations.literal: and further had strong soldiers beat them in relays.
translations.idiomatic: and further had strong soldiers beat them in relays.

translations.idiomatic: Prisoners generally could not endure it and therefore falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 吏持此以為能。

translations.literal: Officials regarded this as competence.
translations.idiomatic: Officials regarded this as competence.

translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he was grieved and decreed that unless there was clear evidence of great treason, those who did not confess might not be placed in heavy cangues.

sentences.zh: 律：「枉法十匹，義贓二百匹大辟。

translations.idiomatic: The law stated: "Perverting the law for ten bolts of goods brought capital punishment; improper gifts of two hundred bolts brought capital punishment."

sentences.zh: 」至八年，始班祿制，更定義贓一匹，枉法無多少皆死。

translations.literal: By the eighth year, the salary system was first instituted, and improper gifts were redefined at one bolt; perverting the law, regardless of amount, all brought death.
translations.idiomatic: By the eighth year the salary system was instituted, improper gifts were redefined at one bolt, and perverting the law, regardless of amount, brought death.

sentences.zh: 是秋遣使者巡行天下，糾守宰之不法，坐贓死者四十餘人。

translations.literal: That autumn envoys were sent to tour the realm and investigate unlawful conduct by prefects and governors; more than forty who were convicted of bribery were executed.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn envoys were sent to tour the realm and investigate unlawful conduct by prefects and governors; more than forty convicted of bribery were executed.

sentences.zh: 食祿者跼蹐，賕謁之路殆絕。

translations.literal: Those who received salaries walked in fear, and the roads of bribery petitions were nearly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Salaried officials lived in fear, and the paths of bribery were nearly cut off.

sentences.zh: 帝哀矜庶獄，至於奏讞，率從降恕，全命徙邊，歲以千計。

translations.literal: The emperor showed compassion for the common prisons; even in memorials on criminal cases he generally granted leniency and reduction, sparing lives and banishing to the frontier, numbering in the thousands each year.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed compassion for the common prisons; even in memorials on criminal cases he generally granted leniency, sparing lives and banishing offenders to the frontier by the thousands each year.

sentences.zh: 京師決死獄，歲竟不過五六，州鎮亦簡。

translations.literal: Capital cases decided in the capital did not exceed five or six in a year, and the provinces and garrisons were likewise restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Capital cases decided in the capital did not exceed five or six in a year, and the provinces and garrisons were likewise restrained.

translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year, an edict said: "Among the three thousand offenses, none is greater than unfilial conduct, yet the law for disrespect toward parents stops at head-shaving punishment."

translations.literal: This is not right in principle.

translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: "Previously We ordered the dukes and ministers to discuss and fix the penal code, yet clan execution still remained in the statutes, contrary to the Book of Zhou's doctrine that father and son bear different punishments."

sentences.zh: 推古求情，意甚無取。

translations.literal: Seeking antiquity and examining sentiment, this is greatly undesirable.
translations.idiomatic: Examining antiquity and human sentiment, this is greatly undesirable.

sentences.zh: 可更議之，刪除繁酷。

translations.literal: It may be discussed again and redundant harshness deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Discuss it again and delete redundant harshness.

sentences.zh: 」秋八月詔曰：「律文刑限三年，便入極默。

translations.literal: For the same type of offense there is no half-standard of comparison, yet crimes differ between death and life.

sentences.zh: 可詳案律條，諸有此類，更一刊定。

translations.idiomatic: Examine the legal articles in detail; wherever such cases occur, revise them anew.

sentences.zh: 」冬十月，復詔公卿令參議之。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month of winter an edict again ordered the dukes and ministers to discuss it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an edict again ordered the dukes and ministers to discuss it jointly.

sentences.zh: 十二年詔：「犯死罪，若父母、祖父母年老，更無成人子孫，又無期親者，仰案後列奏以待報，著之令格。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth year an edict said: "For those condemned to death, if their fathers and mothers or grandfathers and grandmothers are old and there are no adult sons or grandsons, and no relatives within the mourning period, the case shall be submitted for later listing and await reply; let this be written into the ordinances."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year an edict said: "For those condemned to death, if their parents or grandparents are old and there are no adult sons or grandsons and no relatives within the mourning period, the case shall be submitted for later listing and await imperial reply; let this be written into the ordinances."

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，意在寬政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded to the throne, his intent lay in lenient government.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded to the throne, his intent was lenient government.

sentences.zh: 正始元年冬，詔曰：「議獄定律，有國攸慎，輕重損益，世或不同。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Zhengshi, an edict said: "Deliberating cases and fixing the law are matters a state must treat with caution; the weight, lightening, addition, and reduction of punishments differ from age to age."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Zhengshi, an edict said: "Deliberating cases and fixing the law are matters a state must treat with caution; the weight, lightening, addition, and reduction of punishments differ from age to age."

sentences.zh: 先朝垂心典憲，刊革令軌，但時屬征役，未之詳究，施於時用，猶致疑舛。

translations.literal: The former court devoted care to the statutes and laws and revised the ordinances, but the times were marked by campaigns and corvée labor, and they were not examined in detail; applied in practice, they still led to doubt and error.
translations.idiomatic: The former court devoted care to the statutes and laws and revised the ordinances, but the times were marked by campaigns and corvée labor and they were not examined in detail; in practice they still led to doubt and error.

sentences.zh: 尚書門下可於中書外省論律令。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing and the Department of the Gate may discuss the statutes and commands at the outer office of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing and the Department of the Gate may discuss the statutes and commands at the outer office of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 諸有疑事，斟酌新舊，更加思理，增減上下，必令周備，隨有所立，別以申聞。

translations.literal: Wherever there are doubtful matters, weigh the old and new, reflect further, add or reduce as above or below, and make them fully complete; whatever is established shall be reported separately.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever there are doubtful matters, weigh the old and new, reflect further, adjust severity as needed, and make the code fully complete; report separately whatever is established.

sentences.zh: 庶於循變協時，永作通制。」

translations.literal: Thus in following change and harmonizing with the times, it may forever serve as a universal system."
translations.idiomatic: Thus, by following change and harmonizing with the times, it may forever serve as a universal system."

sentences.zh: 永平元年秋七月，詔尚書檢枷杖大小違制之由，科其罪失。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the first year of Yongping, an edict ordered the Masters of Writing to inspect the reasons why cangues and cudgels of improper size violated regulations, and to assess the offenses and faults.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongping, an edict ordered the Masters of Writing to investigate why cangues and cudgels of improper size violated regulations and to assess the offenses involved.

sentences.zh: 尚書令高肇，尚書僕射、清河王懌，尚書邢巒，尚書李平，尚書、江陽王繼等奏曰：「臣等聞王者繼天子物，為民父母，導之以德化，齊之以刑法，小大必以情，哀矜而勿喜，務於三訊五聽，不以木石定獄。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Gao Zhao, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Prince Yi of Qinghe, Master of Writing Xing Luan, Master of Writing Li Ping, Master of Writing and Prince Ji of Jiangyang, and others memorialized saying: "We have heard that the king continues Heaven's charge, serves as father and mother to the people, guides them with moral transformation and aligns them with penal law; great and small must follow circumstance, show compassion and not rejoice, strive for the three interrogations and five hearings, and not fix cases by wood and stone."
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Gao Zhao, Masters of Writing and Vice Director Prince Yi of Qinghe, Master of Writing Xing Luan, Master of Writing Li Ping, Master of Writing and Prince Ji of Jiangyang, and others memorialized saying: "We have heard that the king continues Heaven's charge, serves as father and mother to the people, guides them with moral transformation and aligns them with penal law; great and small must follow circumstance, show compassion and not exult, strive for the three interrogations and five hearings, and not fix cases by wood and stone."

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下子愛蒼生，恩侔天地，疏網改祝，仁過商后。

translations.literal: We respectfully consider that Your Majesty loves the common people as children, with grace equal to Heaven and Earth, loosens the net and changes blessings, and benevolence surpasses the queen of Shang.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully consider that Your Majesty loves the common people as children, with grace equal to Heaven and Earth, loosens the penal net and changes blessings, and whose benevolence surpasses that of the Shang rulers.

sentences.zh: 以枷杖之非度，愍民命之或傷，爰降慈旨，廣垂昭恤。

translations.literal: Because cangues and cudgels exceeded proper measure, pitying that people's lives might be harmed, therefore You descended a merciful edict, broadly extending clear clemency.
translations.idiomatic: Because cangues and cudgels exceeded proper limits, and pitying the harm done to people's lives, Your Majesty issued a merciful edict extending broad clemency.

sentences.zh: 雖有虞慎獄之深，漢文惻隱之至，亦未可共日而言矣。

translations.literal: Even Yu the Shun's depth in careful judging of prisons and Emperor Wen of Han's utmost compassion cannot be spoken of on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Even Yu the Shun's scrupulousness in judging cases and Emperor Wen of Han's deep compassion cannot be mentioned in the same breath.

sentences.zh: 謹案獄官令：諸察獄，先備五聽之理，盡求情之意，又驗諸證信，事多疑似，猶不首實者，然後加以拷掠；

translations.literal: We respectfully consult the prison officials' ordinance: for all who examine prisons, first prepare the principles of the five hearings, exhaust the intent of seeking truth, then verify all evidence, and only when matters are much in doubt and the accused still does not confess truthfully, then apply beating under interrogation;
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully cite the ordinance on prison officials: when examining cases, one must first apply the principles of the five hearings and exhaust every means of discerning the truth, verify all evidence, and only when matters remain doubtful and the accused still will not confess may beating under interrogation be applied;

sentences.zh: 諸犯□年刑已上枷鎖，流徙已上，增以杻械。

translations.literal: All who commit □ year-punishment or higher are cangued and locked; for exile or banishment or higher, shackles and fetters are added.
translations.idiomatic: All offenders sentenced to fixed-term punishment (□ year-punishment) or heavier are to wear cangues and chains; for exile or banishment and above, shackles and fetters are added.

sentences.zh: 迭用不俱。

translations.literal: Use alternately, not together.
translations.idiomatic: They are to be applied alternately, not simultaneously.

sentences.zh: 非大逆外叛之罪，皆不大枷、高杻、重械，又無用石之文。

translations.literal: For crimes other than great treason and foreign rebellion, none uses large cangues, high shackles, or heavy fetters; nor is there any text about using stones.
translations.idiomatic: Except for great treason and foreign rebellion, none may use heavy cangues, high shackles, or severe fetters, and the law contains no provision for using stones.

translations.literal: Yet judges in the provinces and commanderies, taking occasion to increase them, made this a constant practice.

sentences.zh: 進乖五聽，退違令文，誠宜案劾，依旨科處，但踵行已久，計不推坐。

translations.idiomatic: This contradicts the five hearings in practice and violates the ordinance in letter—such conduct truly ought to be investigated and punished according to Your Majesty's intent, but because it has long continued, we do not propose to impute liability retroactively.

sentences.zh: 檢杖之小大，鞭之長短，令有定式，但枷之輕重，先無成制。

translations.literal: Inspection of cudgels' size and whips' length—the ordinance has fixed forms; but the weight of cangues previously had no established rule.
translations.idiomatic: The ordinance prescribes fixed dimensions for cudgels and whips, but no established standard previously existed for the weight of cangues.

sentences.zh: 臣等參量，造大枷長一丈三尺，喉下長一丈，通頰木各方五寸，以擬大逆外叛；

translations.literal: We ministers estimate and propose: make large cangues thirteen chi long, one chi below the throat, with connecting cheek-wood five cun square on each side, to correspond to great treason and foreign rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: We propose establishing large cangues thirteen chi in length, one chi below the throat, with connecting cheek-pieces five cun square on each side, for use in cases of great treason and foreign rebellion;

sentences.zh: 杻械以掌流刑已上。

translations.literal: Shackles and fetters to govern exile punishment and above.
translations.idiomatic: Shackles and fetters are reserved for exile punishments and above.

sentences.zh: 諸臺、寺、州、郡大枷，請悉焚之。

translations.literal: All large cangues in the ministries, courts, provinces, and commanderies—we request that they all be burned.
translations.idiomatic: We request that all heavy cangues in the ministries, courts, provinces, and commanderies be destroyed by fire.

sentences.zh: 枷本掌囚，非拷訊所用。

translations.literal: Cangues originally govern detention of prisoners, not tools for interrogation under torture.
translations.idiomatic: Cangues were originally meant to restrain prisoners, not for use in interrogation by torture.

sentences.zh: 從今斷獄，皆依令盡聽訊之理，量人強弱，加之拷掠，不聽非法拷人，兼以拷石。

translations.literal: From now on in deciding cases, all shall follow the ordinance's full principles of listening and examining, measure the person's strength or weakness in applying beating under interrogation, and not permit illegal torture of persons, including beating with stones.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth in deciding cases, all shall follow the ordinance's full principles of hearing and examination, adjusting beating under interrogation to the prisoner's strength, and illegal torture—including beating with stones—shall not be permitted.
